title: ICE Shoots and Kills Houston Construction Worker Lorenzo Salgado Araujo
excerpt: An ICE officer fatally shot 52-year-old Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, a Mexican national driving his construction crew to a job site in Houston's Magnolia Park neighborhood. DHS alleged he rammed an ICE vehicle; witnesses and family disputed the account.
content:
On July 7, 2026, Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, a 52-year-old Mexican national who had lived in the United States for decades, was fatally shot by an ICE officer as he drove his work crew to a construction site in Houston's East End.

ICE said it was targeting two Guatemalan men riding in a similar white van. According to a CNN source with preliminary knowledge of the incident, Salgado Araujo was not the intended target of the enforcement operation. DHS nonetheless claimed he rammed an ICE vehicle and "weaponized his vehicle in an attempt to run over a law enforcement officer."

  • The agents involved were not wearing body cameras at the time of the shooting.
  • All three passengers in the van disputed DHS's account in sworn court statements.
  • The shooting set off protests across Houston and renewed national debate about ICE use-of-force training and accountability.
  • Multiple investigations were opened: FBI, Texas Rangers, and the Harris County District Attorney's Office.

The killing was described by AP as "at least the eighth death during the Trump administration's immigration enforcement campaign."
